title: 2.2 Detecting radiation, half-life, uses and safety

1.title: Question: how can we detect what we cannot see?

q.Q1: Q1. A GM tube reads 45 counts per minute near a source; the background is 15 counts per minute. What is the count rate from the source?

q.Q3: Q3. The count rate of a source falls from 640 to 80 counts per minute in 15 minutes. Calculate the half-life.

q.Q5: Q5. Explain why a tracer used inside a patient's body should be a gamma emitter with a short half-life.

q.Q6: Q6. State three precautions taken by workers who handle radioactive sources.
q.Q7: Q7. Why is an alpha source very dangerous if swallowed but fairly safe outside the body?
